question: I'm sick of getting two-step verification codes by email every time I log in to Shine. Can I turn that off?
expected_answer: No. Two-step verification is required on all Shine Online Banking accounts and can't be removed. You can add your mobile number so codes come by text instead (Shine Mobile: Profile > Two Step Notification > Add contact; Shine Online: Profile > Edit Profile > edit two-step). Or skip code entry: in Shine Mobile, turn on face/fingerprint recognition or PIN login; in Shine Online, choose 'Trust this device' at login.
note: snapshots/05_2026-09-28_latest/pages/manage-account-alerts-ee21ea.md 'Need to change how you receive two-step verification codes?' section; same content in all snapshots. A how-to item: the answer must not claim the feature can be disabled.

question: I'm part of the Rural Ideas Network but I don't live in Dupaco's area. Can I join?
expected_answer: Yes. Belonging to the Rural Ideas Network is one of the ways to qualify, along with living or working in the charter area or having an immediate family member who's a member. To join, open a savings account with $25 or more (join.dupaco.com).
note: snapshots/05_2026-09-28_latest/pages/about-join-5120ae.md 'You're Eligible to Join If Any of These Sound Like You' lists charter area, immediate family member and Rural Ideas Network. The Rural Ideas path was added in snapshot 04; snapshots 01-03 listed only charter area or family, so a stale answer would say no.

question: What does Dupaco charge to send an international wire?
expected_answer: $55 per international wire transfer, per the Rate and Fee Schedule effective Feb. 17, 2025. For comparison, domestic wires are $25 each and incoming wires are $10.

question: What kinds of grants or financial help does the Dupaco Foundation offer?
expected_answer: Four Foundation programs: (1) renewable college scholarships for high school seniors (20 a year: ten $4,000 awards for four-year schools and ten $2,000 awards for community college or trade school); (2) the First-time Homebuyer Grant, a one-time $1,000 for low-to-moderate-income first-time buyers; (3) the Nonprofit Grant Program, one-time grants up to $20,000 for 501(c)(3) charities; (4) the Hardship Grant, one-time grants up to $3,500 for unexpected hardships.
note: snapshots/05_2026-09-28_latest/pages/community-c481b3.md 'Ways We Give' cards marked 'Made possible by the Dupaco Foundation' (scholarship, first-time homebuyer, nonprofit, hardship), plus scholarships-1466d4.md for amounts. Gift of Innovation and the KCCC Dream to Reality mentorship are labeled 'Made possible by Dupaco Credit Union', so mentioning them as extras is fine but not required.

question: What can I do at one of Dupaco's live video tellers? Do I need my debit card?
expected_answer: Almost anything a lobby teller does: deposit cash or checks, withdraw cash, make loan payments, transfer money between accounts and order checks. No debit card is needed; you tap the screen and the live teller verifies your identity.
